title: Adaptive scale-reservoir + vectorized INT8 shim with KV coalescer for hybrid-precision paths
author: Maya Rodriguez
release_notes: Introduces an adaptive scale-reservoir and an INT8->FP8 compatibility shim plus a KV cache coalescer. Improves hybrid-precision throughput and reduces p99 latency for short- and medium-context workloads. No API changes; rollout as canary to Dedicated tier then staged to Hosted.
description: Motivation: Production workloads with mixed INT8/FP8 layers pay a high cost on repeated dequant/requant cycles and small-prefix KV cache lookups. This PR implements two orthogonal optimizations: (1) a 'scale-reservoir' that maintains compact shared per-layer scale state and serves micro-requantized buffers to downstream kernels, avoiding full dequant paths for short-lived tensors, and (2) a vectorized INT8 compatibility shim that allows FP8 kernels to accept requantized INT8 input without a heavyweight convert. Additionally, we add a KV coalescer in the cache layer to merge adjacent small prefix lookups into fewer GPU uploads and a scheduler hook so the continuous-batcher prefers reservoir-warm slices when possible. Key user-visible outcomes: (a) lower per-token GPU compute when hybrid-precision models are used, (b) fewer GPU memory transfers for KV-prefetch patterns common to chat-like workloads, and (c) safe rollback via a feature flag and a canary rollout path. Changes: new runtime/kernels/int8_shim.cpp/h — vectorized shim and dispatch paths; runtime/scheduler/reservoir_scheduler.cpp/h — scheduler scoring, reservoir lifecycle; runtime/cache/kv_coalescer.cpp/h — prefix coalescing logic and metrics; runtime/loader/quant_hints.cc — model loader exposes per-layer scale hint metadata; runtime/tests/bench_int8_shim.py and runtime/tests/test_kv_coalescer.cc — unit and microbench harnesses; docs/perf/benchmarks/int8_reservoir.md — reproducible commands and plotting. Benchmarks: microbench on A100 and H100 with batch sizes and sequence lengths representative of customer chat workloads (seq_len=16 and seq_len=96) show 12-18% median throughput uplift and 6-9% reduction in p99 latency for the INT8/FP8 mixed model we used as a proxy. End-to-end token-cost simulation on Dedicated workloads indicates a ~10% token compute cost reduction under the tested profile. Compatibility and safety: feature gated by runtime flag REDWOOD_INT8_RESERVOIR; shim only enabled when model metadata includes 'quant_scale_hint'. KV coalescer has heuristic thresholds and a CI test asserting no semantic change in prefix lookups. Rollout: canary on 5% Dedicated capacity for 72 hours, expand to 25% then full rollout if regression-free. See linked Linear ENG-4721 for rollout playbook. Checklist: implement kernels and scheduler hooks, add unit and perf tests, document benchmark steps, add feature flag, run security review for new allocation path.

benchmark_summary: A100 (p3) seq=16: throughput +12% median, p99 -6% ; seq=96: throughput +18% median, p99 -9%. H100 similar profile but +1-2% higher throughput uplift. KV coalescer reduced small-upload GPU transfers by ~34% in our trace-driven sim.
rollout_plan: Canary 5% Dedicated for 72h -> evaluate p95/p99 latency + error budget -> 25% for 48h -> full. Feature toggles for immediate rollback. Operator runbook in ENG-4721.
notes: No customer-facing API changes. Observability added: reservoir.hit_ratio, kv_coalesce_count, shim_dispatch_latency. Wanted to keep change surface minimal to facilitate fast rollback if downstream regressions observed.
